discussion_comments.comment_body:
These are globally scoped and not a function. It also is not very adaptable.

Using the date object and a function you can also get some error checking should something go wrong(return undefined or adopt other methods such as allowing to bubble, up to choice)

Possible replacement:

```js
const toEnglishDate = (time) => {try{return new Date(time).toISOString().split('T')[0].replace(/-/g, '/')}catch(e){return}}
```

discussion_comments.comment_body:
For a version that the developer must handle the errors of themselves(fails on invalid date, not a Maybe):

```js
const toEnglishDate = (time) => new Date(time).toISOString().split('T')[0].replace(/-/g, '/')
```

We are not handling bad input in most snippets, so I don't think we should make this change here. It's better to allow the method to just throw an error and let developers handle it, instead of exiting unexpectedly like that.
I don't think the changes make it exit unexpectedly, only when it reaches the end of the list, as is the expected behaviour.
